comments.author: alwillis
comments.why: Flutter keynote on native look and feel across platforms
comments.text: There is no framework to make apps look iOSish on iOS and Androidish on Android. Back to native programming, I guess. Google's Flutter certainly creates apps (using mostly web technologies) that have the correct look and feel for Android and iOS from the same codebase. comments.author: fharper1961
comments.story: The Cost of Native Mobile App Development Is Too Damn High
comments.why: Flutter keynote for building iOS and Android apps from one codebase
comments.text: From what I've heard React Native doesn't yet handle lists containing many views without rendering the entire list. I'm looking into Flutter/Dart from Google for building iOS/Android apps from the same codebase. The SDK is still alpha so there are still rough edges, but I've created a POC app and have been able to run it on both platforms. I'm very pleased with the results so far. [LINK] [VIDEO]

comments.author: mraleph
comments.story: Flutter doesn’t need Kotlin (or anything else)
comments.why: Early demo of Flutter mimicking platform conventions
comments.text: Flutter has the builtin ability to mimic platform conventions (Android on Android, iOS on iOS), which includes scrolling, animations, fonts, etc. If you have an Android phone you can download Flutter Gallery app from Play Store, go to the menu and flip behavior from Android to iOS. Suddenly you have an app that behaves like an iOS app. Here is a demo like that from the early days: [VIDEO]
